entities.summary: Lars Herminius Aquilinus was consul in 448 BC with Titus Verginius Tricostus Caeliomontanus. Their consular term was marked by a relatively peaceful coexistence between the patricians and the plebeians, as neither consul took sides in the conflict between these two factions. This peaceful period allowed for trade, cultural exchange, and the development of the Roman Republic's infrastructure. Lars Herminius Aquilinus played a key role in shaping the early Roman Republic's legal and political systems. He was a prominent figure in the Curia, Rome's legislative body, and worked closely with the Roman Senate to establish the foundations of the Roman Republic's governance. The legacy of Lars Herminius Aquilinus can be seen in the development of Roman law and the institution of the consulship, which remained an important part of the Roman Republic's political structure until the end of the Roman Empire. The Roman historian Livy praised Lars Herminius Aquilinus for his wisdom and integrity, stating that he was 'a man of great virtue and excellent character'.
